meta.title: Ten Years of Search Guard — The 2016 Time Machine
meta.description: Our first licence sold in September 2016. One question for every year since — TikTok, the GDPR, SolarWinds, and the version number we skipped. About 90 seconds.
meta.ogTitle: Ten years ago, a stranger paid for software we'd written
meta.ogDescription: They're still with us. One question for every year since — most people miss the one about the GDPR.

hero.headline:
Ten years ago, a stranger paid for software we'd written.
They're still with us.
hero.text: That invoice is the birthday we're counting — not a founding date, not a first commit. Below is the decade that followed, and one question for every year of it.

intro.instruction: One question for every year, 2016 to 2025. Every right answer lays a brick — ten bricks build the 10.
intro.cookbook: The cookbook waiting at the end is a real one: beloved home recipes from the people who build Search Guard, collected over ten years of offsites. Yours for an email, whatever you score.
intro.prize: And a perfect ten? That puts you in the draw for a €110 LEGO gift card.
intro.meta: 10 questions · about 90 seconds · no sign-up to play · a cookbook at the end

questions.q: One of these launched in the same month as our first licence. Which?
opts: Douyin — the app that became TikTok
questions.reveal: Douyin launched on 20 September 2016, originally called A.me. TikTok didn't reach the rest of the world until September 2017. So Search Guard and TikTok are almost exactly the same age.

questions.q: Search Guard finally got a face in January 2017. What shipped?
questions.reveal: Until then Search Guard was configured entirely without a UI. The Kibana plugin arrived in January 2017; the TLS Tool followed in February 2018.

questions.q: The GDPR became fully enforceable across the EU — the deadline every company scrambled for. In which year?
questions.reveal: 25 May 2018 was the day it took full effect and the inboxes overflowed. It had actually been adopted back in 2016, so the deadline was never really a surprise — though plenty of last-minute emails suggested otherwise.

questions.q: We started building something in May 2019 that let Elasticsearch tell you when things go wrong. What?
questions.reveal: Signals began in May 2019, went to beta that December, and reached GA in January 2020. Before it, most teams found out about a problem when somebody complained.

questions.q: Which supply-chain breach, disclosed in December 2020, had every security team re-reading their vendor list?
questions.reveal: Disclosed 13 December 2020. Around 18,000 organisations downloaded the compromised update, and the attackers had been inside for eight to nine months before anyone noticed. Heartbleed was 2014; Log4Shell was still a year away.

questions.q: Elasticsearch 7.10.2 has a particular place in history. Why?
opts: It was the fastest release ever benchmarked
It was the last version under the Apache 2 licence
It was the first version to support Kubernetes
questions.reveal: Elastic moved to the SSPL in 2021, making 7.10.2 the last Apache-2 licensed release. We announced long-term support for it that June, because a lot of people needed somewhere to stand.

questions.q: What did we call the next generation of Search Guard, GA in August 2022?
questions.reveal: Search Guard FLX went GA in August 2022 after three betas, and shipped for Elasticsearch 8 the following month.

questions.q: One feature returned to FLX in August 2023, seven years after it first appeared in Search Guard 5. Which?
questions.reveal: Audit logging shipped in Search Guard 5 in November 2016 and came back in FLX 1.3.0 in August 2023. Rebuilding a product means earning your own features back one at a time.
questions.hint: Both dates are on our timeline →

questions.q: In July 2024 a single software update took down an estimated 8.5 million computers worldwide — grounding flights and stalling hospitals. Whose update was it?
questions.reveal: On 19 July 2024 a faulty CrowdStrike Falcon update blue-screened around 8.5 million Windows machines — the largest IT outage in history, and no attacker involved. Just a security tool doing more damage than the threats it was guarding against. Test what you push to production.

questions.q: What went into technical preview in March 2025?
questions.reveal: Encryption at Rest, which encrypts the data Elasticsearch writes to disk — indices, translogs and all. Anomaly Detection started the month before, and Automated Index Management back in February 2024.

lines.10: Flawless. You were paying attention in 2016 — and you've read our timeline.
lines.9: Nearly perfect. One slip in a decade is forgivable.
lines.8: Strong. You clearly lived through 2016 with your eyes open.
lines.7: Solid. Most of that decade stuck.
lines.6: Respectable. 2016 was a long time ago.
lines.5: Half marks — which, for a year that felt this long, is fair.
lines.3: You may have been busy that decade.
lines.1: One right. We admire the commitment to guessing.
lines.0: Perfectly wrong throughout. That takes a kind of talent.
